newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepali leader leaves on visit to Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: Nepali leader leaves on visit to Pakistan.

text.p: Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba left for a five-day official visit to Pakistan on Friday, the first by a Nepali leader in 13 years.
"It is a goodwill visit," Deuba told reporters before leaving Kathmandu for the Pakistani capital Islamabad.
He said he would discuss trade and investment with his Pakistani counterpart, Benazir Bhutto, and other government leaders.
Deuba was accompanied by Foreign Minister Prakash Chandra Lohani and a team of Nepali businessmen.
Deuba planned to press Pakistan for softer terms to boost bilateral trade, a Foreign Ministry spokesman said on Thursday.
Two-way trade totalled 138 million rupees ($2.4 million) last year. Of that, Nepal had a deficit of 132 million rupees ($2.3 million).
Deuba was also scheduled to visit Lahore and Karachi, the business capital and port city in southern Pakistan where he will invite investors to Nepal, officials said.
Nepali businessmen are seeking an overland transit route through India.

Nepal and Pakistan, members of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC), do not have contiguous borders. Trade between them is routed through Singapore, which is expensive and delays shipments, officials said.
